long_biography.plain_text:
At Corp, Pablo Castro Saez helped develop homes that buyers could customise, from room layouts to kitchen furnishings and finishes. He trained in law, with postgraduate study in urban planning and real estate law. The company attracted buyers willing to reserve apartments before construction was complete.

The company’s economics relied on reasonable margins and steady sales, while retained annual profits financed further land purchases. Castro and his business partner recruited Fernando Cirera to run the operation. Corp also undertook developments for other owners, including a residential tower commissioned by Altamira in Barcelona’s Poblenou district.

Sources give differing Corp founding years (2007, 2008 and 2009). The biographies omit the disputed year. They also avoid the precise terms and value of the Spanish exit, present stakes in Corp and uncompleted HueHub forecasts.

The family-business starting advantage is established, but no source quantifies initial capital or demonstrates inheritance of Corp’s core assets. The classification does not imply an independent start or a known absence of every family transfer.

S6’s old rectification link returned 404, but focused searches located the accessible 14 February 2023 statement at S11. It disputes nightclub allegations and the portrayal of Gabriel and Maria Trinidad’s management; it does not specifically contest the passages about Pau’s parentage, Corp co-founding or former family-company role. Non-objection is not confirmation. Independent The Real Deal reporting (S4) supports involvement in his father’s nightclub business, and the wealth-origin score remains a conservative 81. None of the disputed allegations or current family-management claims enters the biographies or tags.

Residential development is the minimum useful active set.
